name: Dash0
summary: Dash0 is a New York/Berlin OpenTelemetry-native observability vendor, a unicorn since its $110M Series B (Mar 2026), whose Agent0 AI agents read customer telemetry and act on it (root cause, alerts, deployments, security response). It is a strong buyer-fit because agents with tool access to production data need runtime control, but as an observability vendor that has said it will acquire in LLM/agent observability and AI security, it could also be a partner or an adjacent competitor to White Circle's Analyze module.
product: Agentic observability platform on OpenTelemetry: SignalStore (logs, metrics, traces, profiles, events, RUM), PromQL/SQL query, AI trace triage, MCP server/CLI/API for agents, and Agent0, a set of specialized agents (AI SRE, observability toil, migration, cost, security, deployment) plus customer-built agents and Automations with configurable guardrails. 750+ customers including Zalando, Taco Bell and The Telegraph.

ai_usage.what: Agent0 agents run in ephemeral sandboxes on customer telemetry, using models on AWS Bedrock/GCP Vertex under zero data retention; tools are scoped and mostly read-only, writes go via pull request; automations trigger from Slack, webhooks and checks and can post to Slack, Linear and GitHub. Also AI trace triage and an MCP server so customers' own agents query the same data.
surfaces: MCP server, CLI and API for third-party agents
Customer-built custom agents on Dash0 infrastructure

headcount.growth_note: Hired a CRO (Nov 2025) and a Head of Growth (Jul 2025); Series B funds US go-to-market. Careers page could not be fetched, so open roles are unconfirmed.

news.title: Dash0 raises $110M Series B at $1B valuation, led by Balderton; funds Agent0 and US go-to-market
Dash0 acquires Polar Signals (continuous profiling incl. GPU/CUDA) into SignalStore and Agent0
TFN: Dash0 becomes a unicorn, plans acquisitions in LLM/agent observability, AI SRE and AI security

compliance.eu_ai_act_exposure: Low to moderate. Not a high-risk use case itself; Berlin-founded with EU customers such as Zalando, so transparency duties for Agent0 and GDPR on telemetry apply.
compliance.notes: SOC 2 Type II; HIPAA BAA available under NDA; GDPR; ISO 27001 and PCI DSS in progress (Q1 2027). Agent0 Security Whitepaper on trust.dash0.com (NDA). Already has sandboxing and tool scoping, so it will compare White Circle to in-house controls.

why_now: On 2026-03-23 Dash0 raised a $110M Series B at $1B, earmarked for Agent0 autonomous agents, customer-built agents and US enterprise go-to-market; on 2026-08-17 it bought Polar Signals, and it has said it will acquire in AI security and LLM/agent observability. Agents that act on production for 750+ customers are scaling now, and its Aug 2026 security overview shows agent controls are being documented for enterprise buyers.
likely_pains: Prompt injection through telemetry: logs, traces and error messages are attacker-influenced text that Agent0 reads and could treat as instructions
Cross-tenant data leakage if an agent or MCP session sees another customer's dataset
Agents taking destructive or out-of-scope actions (Slack posts, GitHub or Linear writes, rollout and deployment decisions) via automations
Enterprise security reviews demanding proof of agent runtime controls beyond sandboxing as US deals grow
Third-party coding agents hitting the MCP server with unvetted queries and exfiltrating data
Hallucinated root causes or fixes shown to customers

metrics.hypothesis: Fewer unsafe agent actions, faster enterprise security reviews and shorter sales cycles for Agent0; zero cross-tenant incidents.

economic_buyer.hypothesis: CTO Benjamin Blackmore or CEO Mirko Novakovic for a platform-level control layer; a security lead if one exists (none found).

decision_criteria.hypothesis: Latency inside agent loops, EU/US data residency, SOC 2/HIPAA, per-tenant policy on tool calls, no training on customer data.

decision_process.hypothesis: Engineering-led evaluation by the Agent0/product team, then security review and exec sign-off; likely a bake-off against building in-house.

paper_process.hypothesis: Vendor security review via trust center (SafeBase), DPA and BAA; startup procurement should be fast.

identify_pain.hypothesis: Agents acting on production for 750+ customers, with prompt injection via telemetry and tool-call safety as the core exposure.

champion.hypothesis: Michele Mancioppi (Head of Product) or the Agent0 engineering lead who owns the agent security whitepaper.

competition.hypothesis: In-house guardrails and sandboxing (already built), cloud guardrails on Bedrock/Vertex, other AI security vendors, and Dash0's own planned AI-security acquisitions.

persona_angles.angle: Agent0 reads logs and traces that attackers can write into, so can I show you how White Circle checks every agent tool call in real time before it touches a customer's Slack, GitHub or deploy pipeline?
Your Automations let customers set guardrails in settings; White Circle lets them write those policies in plain language and enforces them on every input, output and tool call.
As you push Agent0 into US enterprises, security reviews will ask how autonomous agents are controlled, and a named runtime control layer with SOC 2 and HIPAA can shorten that review.
You said the platform will not just monitor but act on production, and proving those actions are controlled is how you win enterprise trust against Datadog.
Your Agent0 whitepaper covers sandboxing and read-only tools; White Circle adds red-team testing and real-time policy checks on what the agent says and does, with an audit trail for your customers.

risks: Possible competitor: Dash0 plans acquisitions in LLM/agent observability and AI security, and White Circle's Analyze module overlaps with LLM observability
Possible partner instead of buyer: AI observability plus AI guardrails is a natural integration (White Circle decisions as OTel traces in Dash0), which may be a better first motion than a sale
Strong in-house controls already (ephemeral sandboxes, scoped read-only tools, PR-gated writes, ZDR models), which weakens urgency
No security leader, CISO or head of AI found publicly, so the buying persona is unclear
Careers page unreachable and no job signals confirmed
Customers are mostly engineering teams rather than regulated end users, so EU AI Act and compliance pull is weak
